A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AnyEdit and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–C. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the equations, nine figures, four tables, and appendix examples without material gaps.

before.justification: V1 reports original knowledge-editing experiments on Llama3-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, including benchmark comparisons, timing measurements, sensitivity analyses, and case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix C, including quantitative benchmark results and qualitative editing examples.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same chunking, token/layer selection, hidden-state optimization, and parameter-update procedure. AnyEdit*, chunking alternatives, and integrations with existing editing methods are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same coverage: UnKEBench, AKEW Counterfact and MQUAKE, and EditEverything's mathematics, code, chemistry, news, and poetry domains. No training or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains FT-L, MEND, ROME, MEMIT, AlphaEdit, and UnKE. The comparator sets in the integration experiments and appendix case studies also match. The newly cited works are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The model configurations, evaluation metrics, preprocessing descriptions, and testing procedures remain unchanged. Section 5.2 still specifies batch size 1 and decoding temperature 0.001, and Appendix A retains the same experimental settings.

E4.justification: Section 3's probability and output-length analyses, Appendix C.3's chunk-size sensitivity analysis, and Appendix C.1's editing case studies retain the same questions, evidence, and findings.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same plus/minus reporting, and the plotted uncertainty displays are unchanged. No run-count, seed, significance-testing, or uncertainty-estimation information is added or removed.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the experimental plots retain identical numerical results. Appendix C's generated examples and qualitative findings also match; no result entries are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 removes the redundant Bayes-rule re-expression in v1 Equation 25, which restates retained Equation 24. The theorem, assumptions, and substantive proof arguments remain unchanged; subsequent equations are renumbered.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the efficacy-barrier argument, autoregressive editing contribution, plug-and-play capability, and claims about handling knowledge of arbitrary length and format.

C2.justification: Interpretations of editing efficacy, generalization, computational overhead, and chunk-size tradeoffs are unchanged. Section 7 retains the same limitations concerning lifelong editing and multimodal knowledge.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same hyperparameters, layer selections, chunk sizes, data-processing information, and single A100 80GB hardware disclosure. The code-access statement is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds a sentence connecting model editing to hallucination mitigation and information injection, citing two newly listed works: Huang et al.'s 'Can knowledge editing really correct hallucinations?' and Chen et al.'s 'Can editing llms inject harm?' The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 changes the affiliation from Bytedance to Douyin Co., Ltd., adds a short related-work sentence, and shortens Appendix B.2's exposition. The section order and nearly all prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All figures and tables retain their designs and content. The added references and shortened proof cause limited paragraph and equation reflow, including moving Appendix B.3's Step 2 from page 16 to page 15.

improvement.justification: The new citations slightly broaden the context, and Appendix B.2 becomes shorter by omitting an equivalent formula. These limited editorial refinements leave the substantive reasoning, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations unchanged, with no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
